title: Coronation Chicken
subtitle: Cold poached chicken in a curried mayonnaise with apricots
excerpt: Cold poached chicken breast stirred through a sauce of mayonnaise, curry powder, mango chutney, and dried apricots. Served in sandwiches, jacket potatoes, or on a bed of lettuce.

recipe.sourceNotes: Coronation Chicken was created by Constance Spry and Rosemary Hume for the banquet following Queen Elizabeth II's coronation in 1953. The original recipe, which they called 'poulet reine Elizabeth', was a cream and curry sauce with cold cooked chicken, apricots, and almonds. The dish was created to be practical for a large formal occasion: it could be made ahead and required no last-minute preparation. It was immediately popular and became one of the most recognisable British dishes of the 20th century. The recipe has evolved considerably from the original, and most modern versions use mayonnaise as the base.

content.text: Poach the chicken gently: a rolling boil will make it tough and stringy. The chicken is done when a skewer inserted in the thickest part meets no resistance. Allow it to cool completely in the poaching liquid for the juiciest result. The sauce can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to two days before mixing with the chicken.

Place the chicken breasts in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Add the bay leaves, peppercorns, and a generous pinch of salt. Bring just to a simmer, then poach over low heat for 15 to 18 minutes until cooked through. Remove from the heat and leave to cool in the liquid for 30 minutes.
Mix together the mayonnaise, yoghurt, mango chutney, curry powder, and lemon juice. Season. Stir in the chopped apricots.
Drain the chicken. Shred or dice into generous pieces. Fold into the sauce. Serve piled into crusty rolls, spooned over a jacket potato, or on a bed of cos lettuce. Scatter with fresh coriander.
